answer: Post-hoc overlap scoring measures how tightly a cluster of agent identities share the same bridge into a settlement river. After each cycle, any group whose lotus coefficient exceeds the 99th percentile is flagged and barred from reward distribution. Each flagged identity pays a fixed two-hundred-token charge deducted from its pending payout at finality. Because detection is retroactive, the cost lands only after the attacker has already spent compute, making additional identities unprofitable.
